title: Launch Momentum Dashboard and Initiative Dependency Mesh for Cross‑Surface Release Trains
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight Launch Momentum Dashboard and a machine-readable Initiative Dependency Mesh to give program managers and engineering leads a single view of launch velocity, blocking dependencies, and risk signals across runtime, console, and API surfaces. The deliverables are: (1) an interactive dashboard (Grafana prototype -> Console panel) that surfaces per-train momentum (progress vs runway, open critical blockers, test/pass rates, capacity reservations), (2) a dependency mesh service (CRON-driven graph + web UI) that tracks parent/sub-issue relationships and indicates ownership conflicts and cross-surface overlaps, and (3) a set of alerting contracts and runbooks (canary gating and rollback triggers) tied to the dashboard signals.

Why now: multiple Q1 launches exposed gaps in cross-team visibility. Teams frequently double-book capacity and miss canary windows because the calendar lives in several spreadsheets and there is no signal-based throttling. This initiative aims to reduce manual coordination overhead and decrease cross-surface launch friction by automating detection and surfacing of conflicts and by giving product owners an at-a-glance momentum metric to decide go/no-go.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dashboard prototype shows per-release-train momentum, open critical blockers, pipeline status (CI/CD pass rate), and a capacity reservation heatmap for next 8 weeks.
- Dependency mesh ingests Linear tickets (PM/ENG/DES) and exposes edges for parent_issue/sub_issues and explicit 'blocks' dependencies; UI highlights ownership conflicts and unknown owners.
- Two alerting contracts implemented: (a) auto-notify when two trains reserve >70% of pooled Dedicated capacity in the same window, (b) flag canary windows with <80% successful shadow traffic tests.
- Runbooks for on-call and release owner that map dashboard signals to actions (throttle, postpone, engage infra).

Scope exclusions: We will not implement enforcement (auto-blocking) in this phase — only detection, alerting, and playbook guidance.

Stakeholders: PM leads (Asha, Maria), Release Engineering (Liam, Priya), Runtime (Tomas), Console (Jordan), Observability (Riley), Design (Nina).
comments: 2026-02-10 — Created ticket. Initial scoping workshop with Release Eng and Observability. Outcome: prioritize dashboard MVP + dependency ingest before automation. Action: ENG to prototype ingest cadence (Tomas + Riley).

2026-02-13 — Design kickoff. Nina shared two layout directions (compact table vs. calendar-first heatmap). Decided to prototype both and test with 3 PMs next week. Links: https://drive.redwood/design/launch-momentum-mocks

2026-02-16 — ENG spike completed (ENG-1842). Tomas implemented a small Linear->graph ingest; discovered rate-limit on Linear API for bulk scans. Workaround: incremental webhook + nightly reconciliation. PR: https://github.com/redwood/release-mesh/pull/42

2026-02-20 — PM sync: agreed on momentum metric formula (weighted score: percent of milestone complete * 0.6 + CI pass rate * 0.3 + blocker severity-adjusted inverse * 0.1). Documented rationale and sample calculations in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PM/Launch+Momentum+Metric

2026-02-25 — Observability instrument plan: Riley to ship three SLIs (momentum-trend, capacity-contention, canary-success-rate) and wire alerts to PagerDuty with a new PD schedule for release-owners. Draft runbook created and assigned for review (Liam).
notes: Risks: Linear API limits, mismatched ownership, and edge cases where capacity is reserved outside tracked systems (manual emails). Mitigations: nightly reconciliation, owner-confirmation step in dashboard, and manual override documented in runbook. Next steps: usability test with 3 PMs (week of 2026-02-29), final MVP signoff by 2026-03-08.
